statement: The random forest's standard settings — 500 trees, each on a bootstrap of every row, mtry floor(√p) for classes and max(floor(p/3),1) for a number, smallest leaf 10 rows for class probabilities and 5 for a number — are randomForest's/ranger's defaults (a true random forest, unlike scikit-learn's regressor default max_features=1.0, which is bagging), and using 10 as a minimum leaf rather than ranger's minimum node size is a stricter but acceptable departure.
regime: prediction; random_forest; every size (standard candidate; kept alone below n_plan 300)
claimed_basis: Liaw & Wiener 2002 (randomForest); Wright & Ziegler 2017 (ranger); Probst, Wright & Boulesteix 2019; RECIPES §2.2.

statement: In a dietary analysis with total energy in the outcome model (standard model, or residual method with energy kept), a nutrient's coefficient estimates a substitution: more of that nutrient in place of the same energy from the energy sources not in the model, at fixed total energy, not the effect of simply eating more of it; with several energy sources in the model, 'everything else' is only the sources left out.
regime: dietary lens; nutrient exposures; a total-energy column in the outcome model; linear model
decision: how every energy-adjusted coefficient, estimand caption and energy finding is read

statement: When the outcome is BMI, adiposity, weight, waist, body fat or diabetes, total energy is plausibly on the causal path from diet composition to the outcome and adiposity causes under-reporting of energy, so conditioning on reported energy can be over-adjustment and collider-stratification bias at once, and adjusted and unadjusted models should both be presented.
regime: dietary lens; energy-related outcome (named or read from values)
decision: the energy card's disputed note, the DISPUTED badge on the energy finding, the adjustment drawer

statement: Tuning candidates should be chosen by the comparison's strictly proper primary loss (squared error, log loss or ranked probability score) pooled over every inner validation row (sum of w*loss / sum of w, survey-weighted under the population answer), not by an average of per-fold scores such as R-squared, and never by AUC or accuracy.
claimed_basis: RECIPES §4.2 'Score' row; MODELING_SEQUENCE ruling 4 (strictly proper primary); RECIPES F5 (RidgeCV averaged per-fold R-squared); §7.3 'tuning on AUC or accuracy' impossible by construction.

statement: For a continuous outcome a held-out score needs at least 100 held-out rows, and for a multiclass or ordinal outcome at least 100 held-out rows in the rarest class or level, to be useful, so below that cross-validation alone is offered first.
regime: continuous, multiclass or ordinal outcome; a 20% holdout below the floor
decision: Order of the split question's options
claimed_basis: Labeled a convention by analogy with the binary 100-event rule; no citation.

statement: The distribution of each person's mean of two 24-hour recalls is narrower than the distribution of usual (long-run average) intake, because averaging two days pulls each person toward the population mean, so percentiles read from it understate the share in both tails.
regime: describing usual intake from one or two 24-hour recalls per person
claimed_basis: NUTRITION_PACK §03; Tooze et al. 2006 (J Am Diet Assoc 106:1575).

statement: Including the outcome in the imputation model is invalid under every goal, including estimating a regression coefficient, because the outcome would then inform its own predictors and bias the coefficients away from zero; blanks in predictors must always be imputed without the outcome.
regime: any goal (describe, estimate or predict) with blanks in predictors
claimed_basis: MODELING_SEQUENCE §2 (blanks); Sisk et al. 2023; BLUEPRINT §12 ruling 4.

statement: When the marginal risk difference or ratio is declared, the unmeasured-confounding E-value is computed on the marginal risk ratio with its bootstrap limits rather than on the conditional odds ratio, since a risk difference has no E-value without its risks.
regime: inference; binary outcome; marginal measure declared

statement: The injection order and the analytical batch along which QC-RLSC fits each feature's drift cannot be settled from the values (a sample number is also all-distinct; a preparation plate or a study group run in blocks also forms contiguous blocks); the guesses are a column named as a run order holding complete distinct numbers, else a whole-number permutation of the row positions, and batch columns named batch/run/plate (2+ levels, each on more than one row, at most n/4 levels), else a column whose levels each occupy one unbroken stretch of the injection order; at most two batch candidates are offered beside 'one curve over the whole run', and the user's choice settles them.
regime: Metabolomics/assay data offered QC-RLSC drift correction.
decision: Columns QC-RLSC uses for drift order and batch.
claimed_basis: MS7 repair; METABOLOMICS_PACK §01 (name-blind reading); KIND_RULES injection_order/batch readings.py:1308, :1330.

statement: For an unpenalized logistic regression fit by maximum likelihood, multiplying any predictor by a positive constant before fitting leaves the out-of-fold predicted probabilities unchanged, so the app does not rescale predictors for this family.
decision: predictor scaling for unpenalized logistic regression
claimed_basis: Equivariance of the maximum-likelihood estimate under linear reparameterization (McCullagh & Nelder 1989).

statement: Rows that are imputed copies of one record (e.g., NHANES DXA's five imputations) are, under inference, each analyzed as a completed dataset and the estimates pooled by Rubin's rules, which carries the imputation's uncertainty.
regime: inference; rows read as imputed copies

statement: Under prediction, internal validation must resample the entire modeling pipeline, so every step learned from data (energy-adjustment residuals, scaling, imputation, PCA loadings, feature ranking and selection, thresholds, tuning) is fit inside each training fold; selecting features on all samples can report near-zero error when no signal exists.
regime: prediction; any table; cross-validation or bootstrap
decision: the fit pipeline (every learned step in-fold) and the split drawers
claimed_basis: CLINICAL_SURVEY_PACK §A5.5 (SETTLED); GENOMICS_PACK §08 (Ambroise & McLachlan 2002); WHAT_EXPLORATION_MAY_DECIDE §5.3 (Hornung 2015; Moscovich & Rosset 2022)
